title: Treat obesity with an approved oral small-molecule GLP-1 agonist

concept.text: Deliver clinically effective incretin-based weight management through a non-peptide oral drug. Orforglipron achieved approval, separating this milestone from oral delivery of peptide semaglutide. Proposed completion test: FDA chronic weight-management approval for an orally administered non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist, supported by randomized phase 3 weight-loss trials lasting approximately 72 weeks. Test set by: FDA; the approved indication covers adults with obesity or overweight and at least one weight-related comorbidity. Reported achieved: FDA approved orforglipron (Foundayo) on 1 April 2026. Overlaps: END-05, PHA-11. Sources given: [FDA Foundayo approval announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-new-molecular-entity-under-national-priority-voucher-program?source=tmtc) ; [FDA Foundayo prescribing information](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/220934Orig1s000lbl.pdf).

page.title: First oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist for obesity
page.definition: An oral drug made from a nonpeptide small molecule activates the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor, the target of a hormone that helps regulate appetite. FDA approved the first such drug, orforglipron, to reduce excess weight and maintain weight loss long term in adults with obesity or with overweight and at least one weight-related condition. Oral semaglutide acts on the same receptor and has the same weight-management use, but its active ingredient is a peptide.

goal.need: In 2024, 940 million adults worldwide lived with obesity. Sustained losses of 5% or more of starting weight can improve metabolic and cardiovascular risk factors. People taking semaglutide for obesity can use a weekly injection or take a daily tablet on an empty stomach and wait at least 30 minutes before food, drink or other oral medicines. Orforglipron gives people who prefer a pill the option to take it with or without food. Treatment accompanies a reduced-calorie diet and increased activity. Gastrointestinal side effects can limit treatment.

completion.title: FDA approves the first oral nonpeptide small-molecule GLP-1 agonist for long-term obesity treatment.
completion.criterion: FDA approves at least one orally administered nonpeptide small molecule that activates the GLP-1 receptor to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction long term in adults with obesity, alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, new drug application approval and approved prescribing information.
completion.threshold_quote: in combination with a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction long term in adults with obesity
completion.basis: FDA approved Foundayo (orforglipron) tablets on 1 April 2026 under NDA 220934 and identifies the drug as the first oral nonpeptide small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist approved for weight management. The label also covers adults with overweight and at least one weight-related condition. Two 72-week randomized trials supported approval. A bioequivalence study linked the capsules used in those trials to the marketed tablets, including the 36 mg capsule and 17.2 mg tablet.

milestones.title: An oral nonpeptide GLP-1 agonist reduces primate food intake at one-sided P < 0.025.
milestones.criterion: After once-daily oral dosing for five days in cynomolgus monkeys, mean food consumption during the 90-minute feeding periods is lower with the agonist than with vehicle. Use a mixed model with animal as a random effect and dose as a fixed effect, with multiplicity-adjusted Dunnett comparisons at one-sided α = 0.025.
milestones.set_by: Chugai and Eli Lilly investigators, Kawai et al., published food-consumption experiment and statistical analysis; this protocol is specific to orforglipron.
milestones.threshold_quote: by one-sided significance level of 2.5% for the order of increase (insulin) or decrease (glucose, mean food consumption)

milestones.title: An oral nonpeptide GLP-1 agonist advances to repeated human dosing after a protocol safety review.
milestones.criterion: Begin repeated oral dosing in healthy participants following review of safety, tolerability, and available drug-exposure and biological-response data through day 5 of the third single-dose cohort. The protocol also permits an earlier start if interim single-dose data show a glucose reduction of approximately 10 to 20 mg/dL at a tolerated dose.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly and Company, NCT03929744, protocol J2A-MC-GZGA(f), sections 5.1 and 10.3.7.
milestones.threshold_quote: Part B may be initiated earlier if approximately 10 to 20 mg/dL glucose-lowering effect is observed at a tolerated dose after reviewing interim data.

milestones.title: An oral nonpeptide GLP-1 agonist beats placebo for weight reduction at 26 weeks in phase 2.
milestones.criterion: In a randomized, double-blind phase 2 trial in adults without diabetes who have obesity or overweight with at least one weight-related condition, at least one once-daily oral dose produces a greater mean percentage reduction in body weight from baseline to week 26 than placebo. Compare each dose with placebo at the two-sided 0.05 level, without multiplicity adjustment, estimating the effect assuming continued treatment.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly and Company, NCT05051579, protocol J2A-MC-GZGI(a), sections 9.1 and 9.3.
milestones.threshold_quote: LY3502970 is superior in percent reduction from baseline in body weight relative to placebo at Week 26

milestones.title: An oral nonpeptide GLP-1 agonist exceeds control weight loss by ≥5 points after one year at maintenance dose.
milestones.criterion: After one year of treatment at the maintenance dosage, the mean percentage reduction from baseline body weight in the oral nonpeptide GLP-1 agonist group exceeds that in the control group by at least 5 percentage points, and the difference is statistically significant. FDA’s draft guidance recommends this benchmark for patients with obesity or with overweight and comorbidities.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, January 2025 draft guidance, section III.B.3.c, Efficacy benchmarks; the recommendation covers weight-reduction drugs generally.
milestones.threshold_quote: the difference in mean percentage weight reduction between the investigational drug and control-treated groups is at least 5% and the difference is statistically significant.

milestones.title: A nonpeptide small molecule increases cyclic AMP through the GLP-1 receptor in cultured cells.
milestones.criterion: In cultured cells expressing the GLP-1 receptor, the compound alone produces a concentration-dependent increase in a cyclic AMP reporter signal and raises intracellular cyclic AMP. Matched cells carrying the reporter without the receptor show no activation by the compound.
milestones.set_by: Functional GLP-1 receptor agonist assays used by Chen and colleagues and by Kawai and colleagues. The matched reporter-cell control follows Chen and colleagues.
milestones.threshold_quote: Agonism was inferred from an increase in reporter signal and also from an increase in cAMP.

milestones.title: FDA accepts an oral nonpeptide GLP-1 agonist application for substantive review for obesity.
milestones.criterion: FDA files a new drug application seeking approval of an oral nonpeptide small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist for long-term weight management in adults with obesity. Filing requires FDA’s determination that the application contains enough information for substantive review.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 314.101(a)(1).
milestones.threshold_quote: FDA has made a threshold determination that the NDA is sufficiently complete to permit a substantive review.

results.finding: LY3502970 increased cAMP in HEK293 cells at 3 human GLP-1R densities. The replicate count for these curves is unstated.
results.detail: The mutant receptor assays used three independent experiments. Those assays tested cells expressing altered receptors.
results.quote: LY3502970 is highly potent at stimulating GLP-1R-induced cAMP accumulation with partial agonist activity relative to native GLP-1

results.finding: Oral LY3502970 reduced mean food intake versus vehicle in 8 cynomolgus monkeys (one-sided Dunnett P < 0.005).
results.detail: LY3502970 was given 180 minutes before feeding. The crossover design used two-day recovery periods.
results.quote: LY3502970 at 0.05 and 0.1 mg/kg decreased food consumption from the first to the fifth days of dosing in a dose-dependent manner

results.finding: Orforglipron produced up to 10.6 percentage points more mean weight loss than placebo at week 26 in a phase 2 trial with 272 adults randomized.
results.detail: For 45 mg versus placebo, the 10.6-point difference exceeds even the sum of the two arm-level 95% CI half-widths (1.5 + 1.6 points), a conservative upper bound for the contrast’s half-width under the same model-based inference.
results.quote:
At week 26, the mean 
change from baseline in body weight ranged from −8.6% to −12.6% across the 
orforglipron dose cohorts and was −2.0% in the placebo group.

results.finding: Orforglipron produced up to 12.3 percentage points more mean weight loss than placebo at week 36 in a trial with 272 adults randomized.
results.quote:
Weight reduction continued through week 36, 
with the placebo-corrected percentage change 
from baseline in body weight ranging from −7.1% 
to −12.3% in the efficacy estimand.

results.finding: In ATTAIN-1 (n=3,127), oral orforglipron 36 mg produced 9.1 percentage points more mean weight loss than placebo after 52 scheduled weeks at maintenance dose.
results.detail: The treatment-regimen estimand included all randomized participants regardless of treatment discontinuation or use of prohibited weight-management treatments.
results.quote:
All orforglipron 
doses were superior to placebo, with a treatment 
difference of −5.5 percentage points (95% CI, 
−6.5 to −4.5) with orforglipron 6 mg, −6.3 per-
centage points (95% CI, −7.3 to −5.4) with orfor-
glipron 12 mg, and −9.1 percentage points (95% 
CI, −10.1 to −8.1) with orforglipron 36 mg 
(P<0.001 for all doses).
